chapter: Newark and first years in Harlem
title: Seminole, Johnny Jones 101 Ranch and bandmaster Edgar Battle
summary: Butler talks of the left-handed pianist/xylophonist Seminole, then of the 101 Ranch show's bandmaster Edgar Battle, and of playing for the New York shows that came through the Newark pit around age eighteen.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Did you encounter this cat named Seminole at that time.
/Seminole was in Sammy Lewis' band with the Bamboo Follies. Yes, Seminole, this man was left-handed and it sounded like two pianos, that he was playing and the same thing with the banjo and guitar.
Sonny Greer heard him play xylophone.

Yes, Seminole -- people coming from out in Maryland, some of them hillbillies of color and Banjo Bernie, there's one of them, why these people--and Snowden;ible) so all right, I stayed in that pit, I stayed in that pit a long, long time and then a circus -- no, it was Johnny Jones 101 Ranch comes to town and a boy, first time I ever seen a
bandmaster of color, fellow was named Edgar Battle, I think he was from Texas, a big tall, very wonderful, range and everything.

Yeah, about that year. Because the songs were 'My Mother's Eyes' and all that stuff, so all right and then now I'm in the pit and all the shows that have come in from New York, I am hearing them and I am playing for them.
